questions.question: Dr. Cherkaoui is a dental surgeon in the public sector. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what is one of the main challenges of public health regarding oral care in Morocco?
options: A sufficient number of dentists in all regions
A chronic shortage of dentists in the public sector, especially in rural areas
A perfectly distributed supply of care across the territory
An overpopulation of dentists in public hospitals
questions.explanation: Morocco faces a shortage of dental surgeons in the public sector, with a very uneven distribution across the territory. According to Article 1 of Decree No. 2.12.507, the ministry may resort to private dentists 'in case of service necessity' for administrative districts suffering from an insufficiency of dental surgeons (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Berrada practices in the private sector but wishes to contribute to public health. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, how can he sign an agreement with the Ministry of Health?
options: By signing an agreement to work part-time in public hospitals
By opening a private practice in a large city
By refusing any partnership with the public sector
By practicing exclusively in the private sector
questions.explanation: Decree No. 2.12.507 allows the Ministry of Health to use, by agreement, private sector dentists to work part-time in public health establishments, notably to ensure the continuity of care (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, under what circumstances can the Ministry of Health call upon private sector dentists?
options: Only in case of an epidemic
In case of service necessity, particularly in areas where the supply of care is insufficient
Only if the dentist requests it
In all regions of Morocco without conditions
questions.explanation: According to Article 1 of Decree No. 2.12.507, the ministry may resort to private dentists 'in case of service necessity' and for administrative districts suffering from an insufficiency of dental surgeons (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Berrada is interested in contracting. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what are the conditions for being contracted?
options: No particular conditions
Be registered with the National Order of Dental Surgeons and not have been subject to a disciplinary sanction
Be under 30 years old
Practice exclusively in rural areas
questions.explanation: Article 6 of Decree No. 2.12.507 stipulates that candidates must be registered with the professional order, not have been subject to an ordinal disciplinary sanction, and not have been convicted of crimes against persons or offenses against public morality (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, how long does a standard agreement last?
options: 1 month
11 months maximum, renewable tacitly 3 times
5 years
Until the dentist's retirement
questions.explanation: In accordance with Article 5 of Decree No. 2.12.507, the agreement is concluded for a maximum duration of eleven months, renewable tacitly three times at most, unless terminated by decision of the administration or at the dentist's request (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what is the remuneration of a contracted dentist for a 4-hour consultation session at the hospital?
options: 100 DH
286 DH
500 DH
questions.explanation: Article 11 of Decree No. 2.12.507 sets the remuneration for a four-hour work session at 286 DH gross (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Cherkaoui, a civil servant, practices at the public hospital. What is the maximum monthly salary that a contracted dentist can receive according to Decree No. 2.12.507?
questions.explanation: Article 11 of Decree No. 2.12.507 sets the maximum monthly gross remuneration at 7,143 DH, payable upon maturity within the limit of 11 months per year (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, to which authority is the contracted dentist subject during their practice in the public sector?
options: Only to the National Order of Dental Surgeons
To the authority of the hierarchical head of the public health establishment
To no authority, they are independent
To the Ministry of Commerce
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Decree No. 2.12.507 specifies that the contracted dentist is subject to the authority of the hierarchical head of the health establishment, the provincial delegate, and the regional director of health, and must sign all technical and administrative documents (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Berrada is under agreement with the ministry. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what are his professional obligations?
options: No particular obligations
He is subject to the same professional obligations as his civil servant counterparts
He is exempt from any administrative obligation
He can freely choose his working hours
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that contracted dentists are subject to the same professional obligations as their civil servant counterparts and to compliance with the internal regulations of the assignment establishments (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Cherkaoui is a civil servant and Dr. Berrada is contracted. Which one can be assigned on-call duty at the hospital according to Decree No. 2.12.507?
options: Only the civil servant
Only the contracted dentist
Both, according to the regulatory procedures in force
Neither
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that when the agreement provides for on-call duty, it must be performed by contracted doctors in accordance with the regulatory procedures applicable to their civil servant counterparts (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what risk does a contracted dentist face for an unjustified absence?
options: A simple warning
Termination of the agreement without notice
A fine of 5,000 DH
A 6-month suspension
questions.explanation: In accordance with Article 10 of Decree No. 2.12.507, any absence during three work sessions, without prior information to the administration and without valid reason, is a cause for termination of the agreement by the administration without notice (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what is the role of professional orders in the contracting process?
options: They have no role
The agreements must be endorsed by the president of the national council of the relevant professional order
They must approve each agreement unanimously
They can refuse any agreement
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that agreements must be endorsed by the president of the national council of the relevant professional order (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Berrada is contracted. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, can he hold several agreements in different regions?
options: Yes, without limitation
Yes, but only within the territorial jurisdiction of the same regional health directorate
No, he can only have one agreement
Yes, if the regions are distant
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Decree No. 2.12.507 specifies that the activities of each contracted dentist and the location(s) where they will be called upon to exercise them must be defined in the agreement, within the territorial jurisdiction of the same regional health directorate (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, is the old decree of 1972 still in force?
options: Yes, it remains applicable
No, Decree No. 2.12.507 repeals it
It is still valid for certain regions
It was replaced by a law
questions.explanation: Article 15 of Decree No. 2.12.507 repeals Decree No. 2-71-641 of January 24, 1972, establishing the special status of doctors, pharmacists, and dental surgeons contracted by the Ministry of Public Health (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to demographic data, how many public sector dental surgeons were there in Morocco around 2005?
questions.explanation: In 2005, there were approximately 202 dental surgeons in the public sector, a ratio of 1 dentist for 148,000 inhabitants, with very significant regional disparities, which motivated the reform of Decree No. 2.12.507.

questions.question: According to professional demographics, in some regions of Morocco, the density of public dentists can be as low as:
options: 1 dentist for 10,000 inhabitants
1 dentist for 100,000 inhabitants
1 dentist for 728,634 inhabitants
1 dentist for 50,000 inhabitants
questions.explanation: The ratio varies from 1 dentist for 12,631 inhabitants to 1 dentist for 728,634 inhabitants depending on the region, illustrating the territorial disparities in access to care that justify the use of contracting provided for by Decree No. 2.12.507.

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, can contracted dentists benefit from travel allowances?
options: No, travel expenses are not covered
Yes, under the conditions and rates set by the regulations
Only if they practice in rural areas
No, they must pay their own travel expenses
questions.explanation: Article 11 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that contracted dentists may, where applicable, benefit from a travel expense allowance at the rates and under the conditions set by the regulatory texts in force (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what is the role of the Ministry of Health in the contracting process?
options: It has no role
It launches calls for applications and defines the districts concerned
It leaves dentists to organize themselves
It imposes agreements on all dentists
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that the use of private sector dentists takes place following a call for applications launched by the Ministry of Health. The districts concerned are defined by ministerial order (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Cherkaoui is a civil servant. According to the texts, are public sector dentists represented within the National Order of Dental Surgeons?
options: No, only private practitioners are represented
Yes, six public sector dentists sit on the national council
Only if they are teachers
They have a single representative
questions.explanation: Six dental surgeons practicing in the public sector sit as ex-officio members of the national council of the Order, including two from State services, two teachers, and two military personnel, in accordance with Law No. 07-05.

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, in case of serious professional misconduct, what procedure is provided for the contracted dentist?
options: A simple summons
Termination of the agreement after consultation with the national council of the relevant professional order
A fine only
No sanction is provided
questions.explanation: Article 10 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that in case of serious professional misconduct, termination of the agreement is taken after consultation with the national council of the relevant professional order (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: Dr. Berrada wishes to be contracted. According to Decree No. 2.12.507, which criterion is prioritized in the case of multiple applications?
options: The candidate's age
The professional address closest to the health establishment
Seniority in the profession
The number of scientific publications
questions.explanation: Article 3 of Decree No. 2.12.507 stipulates that in the event of multiple applications, the doctor whose professional address is closest to the health establishment concerned will be retained (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, can the contracted dentist terminate their agreement at any time?
options: No, termination is impossible
Yes, provided they notify the administration one month in advance
Yes, without notice
Yes, but only in case of illness
questions.explanation: Article 5 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that unless terminated by decision of the administration or at the dentist's request, it is obligatory to notify the other party at least one month before the termination date (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, what does the agreement provide for the dentist in terms of responsibility?
options: They are not responsible for their actions
They are responsible for interns placed under their authority
They are exempt from any responsibility
Responsibility lies solely with the hospital
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that contracted dentists direct and supervise the work of interns and staff placed directly under their authority, and perform themselves the interventions within their competence (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to Decree No. 2.12.507, is the contracted dentist subject to the internal regulations of the establishment where they practice?
options: No, they are subject to their own rules
Yes, they are subject to the internal regulations of the health facility
Only for safety issues
No, they are independent
questions.explanation: Article 9 of Decree No. 2.12.507 provides that contracted dentists are subject to compliance with the internal regulations or administrative rules in use in the assignment establishments (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).

questions.question: According to available information, what is the objective of Decree No. 2.12.507 compared to the old one of 1972?
options: Reduce the number of contracted dentists
Perpetuate recruitment by agreement and revise remuneration conditions
Eliminate any recourse to the private sector
Increase consultation fees
questions.explanation: Decree No. 2.12.507 tends to perpetuate this mode of recruitment by agreement, exclusively to meet the needs of districts suffering from insufficiency, while revising the conditions of contracting and remuneration (Official Bulletin No. 6342 of March 5, 2015).
